Paragraph:
Translation: I can find no means to drive away this grief which is drying up my senses. I will not be able to destroy it even if I win an unrivalled kingdom on the earth with sovereignty like that of the demigods in heaven.

Purport: Although Arjuna was putting forward so many arguments based on knowledge of the principles of religion and moral codes, it appears that he was unable to solve his real problem without the help of the spiritual master, Lord Sri Krsna. He could understand that his so-called knowledge was useless in driving away his problems, which were drying up his whole existence...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna describes the intense, physical toll of his psychological distress ('drying up my senses'). He realizes that no external, material achievement—not even ultimate worldly power—can cure his internal suffering.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: He completely devalues material success as a solution to his existential and psychological crisis, affirming his need for a higher, spiritual intervention.
Outcome/Resolution: He cements his realization that academic knowledge and material prosperity are utterly useless in solving the fundamental problems of existence and deep grief.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.anhedonia: Inability to experience pleasure, Devaluing rewards
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.somatic Symptoms: Physical manifestation of stress ('drying up senses')

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Soka (Profound grief or lamentation that burns the mind and body)
Vairagya (True detachment arising from the realization that material solutions cannot fix spiritual/internal problems)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna hits a profound spiritual realization: material accumulation (economic development, kingdoms) cannot counteract the miseries of material existence (birth, death, grief). Real peace can only be achieved by consulting the absolute truth, reinforcing his submission to Krishna.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Arjuna is describing severe clinical depression characterized by intense somatic symptoms (the physical sensation of his senses 'drying up') and absolute anhedonia. He recognizes that his internal state is so broken that even the greatest external stimulus (unrivalled kingdom) would fail to provide any dopamine or psychological relief.
